briefings.title: 141. Freda的投资札记第2集：Tokenmaxxing、把电机塞进蒸汽机、接力赛变篮球赛、孤独、人的连接
briefings.tldr: The AI industry is transitioning from a period of "Tokenmaxxing" waste to an efficiency-driven era where "better AI builds better AI," shifting business models from per-unit token costs to outcome-based value.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The AI industry is transitioning from a period of "Tokenmaxxing" waste to an efficiency-driven era where "better AI builds better AI," shifting business models from per-unit token costs to outcome-based value.

## The Misleading Nature of "Tokenmaxxing"
*   **The New Unit of Energy:** Freda compares "dollar per token" to the industrial era's "dollar per kilowatt-hour." However, tokens are a misleading metric because "token per task" efficiency varies by orders of magnitude between models.
*   **Quality vs. Quantity:** A superior model might complete a coding task in 100 lines, while a weaker, cheaper model might use thousands of "verbose" lines.
*   **The CFO’s Blind Spot:** Corporate leaders often see skyrocketing token usage as a sign of high employee engagement, when it may actually reflect the inefficiency of the specific AI tool (e.g., a model that requires more tokens to reach the same result).
*   **Usage Trends:** While "Tokenmaxxing" involves significant waste, total AI investment will continue to rise due to the massive expansion of the user base and the number of tasks performed per user.

## The Recursive Competitive Loop: "Better AI Makes Better AI"
*   **The Singularity Point:** The maturation of **Coding Agents** has created a self-improving loop. High-tier AI is now used to develop the next generation of AI, potentially making leading models uncatchable for latecomers.
*   **The Horse vs. Car Analogy:** 
    *   In the early stages, a fast horse (traditional software/search) could keep up with a breakdown-prone car (early AI). 
    *   Once the "AI engine" becomes stable, no "horse" can compete, regardless of its speed.
*   **Strategic Realignment:** Major players are restructuring around this reality.
    *   **OpenAI:** Reorganized into GPT and Coding-focused tracks.
    *   **Google:** Sergey Brin is personally overseeing coding model development.
    *   **Meta:** Internal push to reach State-of-the-Art (SOTA) in coding by year-end.
    *   **xAI:** Publicly acquired Cursor to bolster its coding capabilities.

## Shifting Business Models: From SaaS to Outcome-Based
*   **The Death of the "Per-Seat" Model:** Traditional SaaS (subscription/seat-based) encourages using one vendor to cap costs. AI models are usage-based, which encourages companies to optimize every query by switching between vendors in real-time.
*   **Outcome-Based Pricing:** Companies like **Sierra** (AI customer service) are leading a shift toward charging for successful resolutions rather than compute. 
    *   If the AI solves the problem without a human transfer, they charge; if it fails, they don’t. This aligns the incentives of the vendor and the customer to reduce token waste.
*   **Redefining TAM:** The Total Addressable Market (TAM) for coding isn't just the 50 million developers; it is the $40 trillion global white-collar market. "Coding" in the AI era represents any task where a computer is manipulated to perform work.

## Financial Realities and the "Negative Snowball"
*   **The Profitability Formula:** For model companies to survive the "negative snowball" (where training costs rise faster than margins), the slope of revenue growth must be significantly steeper than the slope of compute costs.
*   **Gigawatt Economics:** The market has systematically underestimated the revenue potential per gigawatt of power. 
    *   Previous estimates suggested $10B in revenue per GW; current data suggests the ceiling for AI revenue generated from that same power could be $50B or higher.
*   **Anthropic’s Growth:** Anthropic achieved an ARR jump from $1B to $5B in less than six months—a faster trajectory than OpenAI during the same period—driven primarily by the explosion in AI-assisted coding.

## Notable Quotes

> "In the beginning, early cars broke down often, and a fast horse could still keep up. But once the car engine stabilizes, no horse—no matter how fast—can ever catch up. That is where we are with AI coding agents." — **Freda Duan**

> "The industry will gradually shift from charging by the token to charging by the result. In areas like customer service, if the AI doesn't solve the problem, you shouldn't pay." — **Freda Duan**

> "We used to think the market for coding models was limited by the number of developers. We were wrong. The real market is every white-collar worker who needs to tell a computer what to do." — **Freda Duan**

briefings.title: Ajay Banga - Karin Rådström - Jesper Brodin | Panel discussion led by Roula Khalaf
briefings.tldr: Effective leadership in legacy organizations requires reconciling a deep respect for institutional history with an aggressive, risk-tolerant push toward simplification and future-readiness.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Effective leadership in legacy organizations requires reconciling a deep respect for institutional history with an aggressive, risk-tolerant push toward simplification and future-readiness.

## The Challenge of Institutional Inertia
* **The "Legacy Cancer":** Ajay Banga highlights the danger of the "we tried that 28 years ago" mentality. He argues that past failures are often irrelevant because variables like market prices and technology have shifted significantly.
* **Complexity Traps:** Karin Rådström noted the inefficiency of having 18 people involved in "very simple topics," emphasizing that organizational bloat often masks a lack of decision-making clarity.
* **The Disruptor’s Blind Spot:** Jesper Brodin reflects on a realization that IKEA had stopped listening to customers, noting that being a historic disruptor can lead to complacency when new disruption (like mobile commerce) arrives.
* **The "One-Third" Rule for Culture Change:** Banga categorizes staff into three groups:
    * **The Supporters:** One-third who want the leader to succeed.
    * **The Resisters:** One-third who actively oppose change.
    * **The Fence-Sitters:** One-third who are waiting to see what happens.
    * **Strategy:** A leader’s job is to win over the middle third to create a two-thirds winning majority; the resisters are rarely winnable.

## Balancing Future Innovation with Historical Legacy
* **Non-Linear Progress:** Brodin argues that the future and the past should not be viewed as a linear trade-off. Leaders must "love the past" but fight to ensure it doesn't stifle the "curiosity of the future."
* **Institutionalized Risk-Taking:**
    * **The "Go Banana" Card:** To combat the fear of making mistakes at IKEA, Brodin issued thousands of cards that essentially co-signed potential failures in advance to encourage entrepreneurship.
    * **American vs. European Mindsets:** Rådström observes a difference in risk-taking between the US and Europe. She advocates for cross-pollinating "American optimism" with "German diligence" to balance boldness with execution.

## Operational Excellence and People Management
* **Banga’s Three Pillars for Management:**
    1. **Done is better than perfect:** Aiming for speed over absolute perfection.
    2. **Fail faster and harder:** Embracing the risk of failure as a learning tool.
    3. **Question everything always:** Constant interrogation of "how things are done."
* **The Five-Minute Rule:** Banga utilizes a simplified four-box feedback system for employees focused on:
    * Positive attributes.
    * Areas for improvement.
    * Three core traits: Urgency, thoughtful risk-taking, and accountability.
    * Long-term career pathing.
    * *Insight:* If a manager cannot fill this out in five minutes, they do not know their employee well enough.
* **"Gardening" the Organization:** Brodin compares organizations to plants—they grow and get more complicated naturally. Leaders must constantly "garden" (prune) the bureaucracy to avoid the need for massive, painful restructurings later.

## The Dual Nature of AI
* **Business Transformation:** Rådström identifies self-driving trucks as a major AI opportunity that could reduce customer costs by 25-30%, requiring more decentralized decision-making as expertise moves away from the boardroom.
* **Societal Risks:** Brodin expresses concern that while AI offers efficiency, it carries risks to human connection. He compares it to the "addiction" of social media, which promised connection but delivered loneliness.
* **The Data Divide:** Banga warns that emerging markets may be left behind in the Large Language Model (LLM) race due to a lack of computing power, electricity, and data infrastructure.
* **National Security:** Banga predicts that "citizen data" will soon be viewed as a high-stakes national security asset, similar to how energy policy is viewed today.

## Notable Quotes

> "The past has proof, but the future doesn't. Therefore you need to invest more than 50 percent of your energy in the future and you need to be prepared to make all sorts of mistakes in it." 
> — **Jesper Brodin**

> "One-third of the people are delighted I am there... One-third of the people just wish I would die tomorrow morning. And one-third of the people are waiting to see what happens to me. Your job as a cultural change leader is to get the last one-third to come on the side of the first one-third." 
> — **Ajay Banga**

> "We guys on the board we're definitely not the experts... [AI] even further puts demands on us to be able to push out decision-making and make sure that people are enabled to drive business who are closest to it." 
> — **Karin Rådström**

> "Life is 50 percent luck. The other 50 percent is what you do with the luck when it comes your way. If you're not willing to take a risk, you're going to be left on that platform and the train will leave." 
> — **Ajay Banga**

briefings.title: Chinese deals & jet fuel: U.S. Ambassador to China & RyanAir CEO - 05/18/26 | Audio Only
briefings.tldr: Following a high-stakes summit in Beijing, U.S. Ambassador David Perdue reported significant trade wins in agriculture and aerospace, though Taiwan remains a contentious "bargaining chip."
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Following a high-stakes summit in Beijing, U.S. Ambassador David Perdue reported significant trade wins in agriculture and aerospace, though Taiwan remains a contentious "bargaining chip." Simultaneously, Ryanair CEO Michael O’Leary warned of looming European airline bankruptcies if current jet fuel spikes and Middle East supply disruptions persist through the summer.

## **U.S.-China Trade & Taiwan Diplomacy**
U.S. Ambassador David Perdue characterized the recent meetings between President Trump and President Xi Jinping as a "historic effort" to correct decades of economic imbalance.

*   **Trade Agreements:**
    *   **Agriculture:** China committed to purchasing $17 billion in U.S. agricultural products annually for the next two years, including the recertification of 400 U.S. beef facilities and the reopening of poultry markets.
    *   **Aerospace:** A major deal was reached for 200 Boeing aircraft and approximately 450 GE engines.
    *   **Future Summits:** President Xi is scheduled to visit the U.S. on September 24, 2026.
*   **The Taiwan "Bargaining Chip":**
    *   **Policy Stance:** Perdue maintains that despite Trump’s "bargaining chip" rhetoric regarding arms sales, U.S. policy (Taiwan Relations Act, Three Communiqués) remains unchanged.
    *   **Security:** The U.S. does not support Taiwanese independence but opposes any "kinetic action" or coercion by China.
*   **China’s Economic Headwinds:** Perdue noted China is facing a "demographic catastrophe" due to the former one-child policy, high youth unemployment, and an unrationalized real estate bubble.

## **Aviation Sector & Jet Fuel Crisis**
With Brent crude hitting $110 and jet fuel spot prices reaching $150/barrel, the airline industry is facing a bifurcated summer.

*   **Ryanair’s Competitive Advantage:**
    *   **Hedging:** CEO Michael O’Leary reported the airline is 80% hedged at $67/barrel through March 2027, insulating it from the current price spike.
    *   **Financial Health:** The carrier is now debt-free with a fleet of 650 aircraft and recently reported a profit of €2.26 billion.
*   **Industry Risks:**
    *   **Bankruptcies:** O’Leary warned that unhedged "low-fare, high-cost" European carriers face collapse if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed through September.
    *   **Consolidation:** The European market is expected to consolidate into four major players: Ryanair and the three legacy families (IAG/BA, Air France-KLM, and Lufthansa).
*   **Regulatory Criticism:** O’Leary called for the abolition of European environmental "ETS" taxes, labeling them "the dumbest taxation known to humankind" for exempting long-haul carriers while taxing short-haul European travelers.

## **Market Pulse & Corporate Shifts**
*   **Berkshire Hathaway (The Abel Era):** Filings revealed Greg Abel’s first major moves as CEO, including new stakes in Delta Airlines and Macy’s, and increased positions in Alphabet and *The New York Times*. Significant exits included Amazon, United Health, and a 35% cut to Chevron.
*   **Monetary Policy:** The Federal Reserve is reportedly "unusually divided" heading into Wednesday’s minutes, with some members pushing for hikes to combat sticky inflation while others favor cuts.
*   **NVIDIA Earnings:** Markets are bracing for Wednesday's results from NVIDIA (trading near $227), viewed as the ultimate bellwether for the AI economy.
*   **Retail Craze:** Swatch stores saw massive crowds and temporary closures for the "Royal Pop" pocket watch, a $400 item retailing for $3,000 on secondary markets.

> "President Trump made it very clear to Xi Jinping in my presence that we're not changing the American policy on Taiwan... We don't support independence, but we also don't want to see coercion across the strait."
— **David Perdue**, U.S. Ambassador to China

> "If oil prices remain up at these levels, if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed until say September or October, there's going to be airline bankruptcies in Europe, like you had Spirit over here in the States."
— **Michael O’Leary**, Ryanair CEO

briefings.title: Dell Tech World 2026 Day 1 Keynote | Unleash the Future of AI
briefings.tldr: Dell Technologies is driving the transition from screen-based AI to physical "intelligence as infrastructure," expanding its AI Factory portfolio with Nvidia to deliver powerful, secure, and hybrid agentic architectures directly to where enterprise data lives.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
Dell Technologies is driving the transition from screen-based AI to physical "intelligence as infrastructure," expanding its AI Factory portfolio with Nvidia to deliver powerful, secure, and hybrid agentic architectures directly to where enterprise data lives.

---

## The Rise of Hybrid and Agentic AI
* **The Shift to Hybrid AI:** Enterprise AI workloads are rapidly moving out of the public cloud to maintain control over data, security, intellectual property, and costs. 
    * A recent Dell Technologies survey reveals that **67% of AI workloads already run outside the cloud** (on-prem, edge, or colocation), and **88% of respondents** run at least one AI workload on-prem.
    * AI infrastructure spending is projected to reach **$3 to $4 trillion globally by 2030**, driven by a massive shift from bits back to physical enterprise hardware.
* **From Assistants to Agentic AI:** Enterprise productivity is transitioning from simple digital assistants (delivering 20% to 30% gains) to autonomous "digital workers." These agents plan, reason, and execute workflows recursively, unlocking **20x to 30x productivity improvements**.
* **Model Choice and Open Ecosystems:** To avoid proprietary lock-in, the Dell Enterprise Hub on Hugging Face has added several major open-source and frontier models, including DeepSeek V4, GLM 5.1, Kimi K2.6, MiniMax M2.7, Gemini 3 (via Google Distributed Cloud on-prem), and SpaceX's Grok.

## Transforming Industry: Eli Lilly and Honeywell Case Studies
* **Eli Lilly (Pharmaceutical Innovation):** CIO Diogo Rau discussed how the 150-year-old pharmaceutical leader utilizes high-performance computing to solve massive scale challenges.
    * **AI-Driven Manufacturing:** Lilly uses high-speed computer vision on packaging lines, capturing 70 photos per vial within milliseconds to instantly detect defects. They also utilize digital twins to optimize manufacturing workflows beyond human capability.
    * **Drug Discovery Supercomputing:** Running the pharmaceutical industry's largest supercomputer with 1,016 GPUs, Lilly has moved beyond simple protein folding (AlphaFold) to model dynamic protein-protein interactions. This allows scientists to design highly selective cancer therapies that target specific diseased cells.
* **Honeywell (Industrial Automation to Autonomy):** CTO Suresh Venkatarayalu outlined Honeywell's evolution into a pure-play automation company powered by its "Forge Platform."
    * **Forge Cognition:** Developed in partnership with Dell and Nvidia, this initiative deploys physical AI servers at industrial sites (such as oil refineries and chemical plants). 
    * **Edge Intelligence:** Running AI models locally at the edge minimizes latency, allowing operators to run real-time simulations to predict manufacturing yield, throughput, and equipment downtime.

## Next-Generation Hardware and Data Infrastructure
* **Dell AI Data Platform:** Engineered to eliminate data bottlenecks, the platform integrates Nvidia’s CuQX libraries natively to deliver **12x faster vector indexing** and **19x faster time to first token**. A new partnership with Starburst utilizes Blackwell GPUs to deliver **6x faster SQL querying**.
* **Dell Exascale Storage:** Introduced as a unified 4-in-1 rack architecture supporting PowerScale, ObjectScale, PowerFlex, and the Lightning File System, it delivers up to **6 terabytes of throughput per second per rack**.
* **Accelerated Compute and Direct Liquid Cooling:**
    * **PowerEdge XE9812:** Built on Nvidia’s NVLink 72, this platform delivers a **10x lower cost per token** than previous generations for massive-scale agentic AI inferencing.
    * **High-Density Racks:** Next-generation PowerEdge XE servers built with Nvidia Ruben and NVLink 8 support up to 144 GPUs per rack with **100% direct liquid cooling**.
    * **PowerCool Solutions:** The PowerCool heat exchanger delivers a **60% reduction in cooling energy consumption**, cutting annual energy costs by one-third.
* **Unmetered Deskside AI:** The new Dell Deskside Agentic AI combines high-performance Precision workstations with Nvidia NemoClaw, allowing developers to build and fine-tune models (ranging from 70 billion to 1 trillion parameters) locally. This solution bypasses public cloud API fees, breaking even in as little as three months.

## Nvidia Partnership and the "Era of Useful AI"
* **Exploding Compute Demands:** Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang noted that because autonomous agents run iteratively and use external tools to complete tasks, the computing requirements for agentic systems have grown **100x to 1,000x** compared to standard user queries.
* **Vera CPU Innovation:** To support agentic workloads, Nvidia developed the Vera CPU, which offers the **highest single-threaded performance in the world** and **3x the memory bandwidth** of traditional CPUs. This ensures databases and agent orchestrators run without bottlenecks.
* **The GB300 Station:** Highlighted as a breakthrough deskside computer, the GB300 Station allows enterprises to run a **1-trillion parameter AI model locally** without latency, security risks, or "token anxiety."

---

## Notable Quotes

> "Intelligence is becoming infrastructure. And just as electricity transformed the world when it left the power plant, AI will transform the world when it leaves the screen."
> — *Michael Dell*

> "In 150 years from now, we're going to have breakthroughs that we couldn't possibly imagine. I think we're on the verge of maybe being able to end disease as we know it... Now the challenge is how do we shorten that distance between the discovery, the imagination, and the execution."
> — *Diogo Rau*

> "A really great engineer in the future is going to be orchestrating a whole bunch of agents, who are going to be orchestrating a whole bunch of sub-agents to do work."
> — *Jensen Huang*

briefings.title: FULL RALLY: Hegseth Joins Ed Gallrein On Kentucky Campaign Trail Against Trump Nemesis Thomas Massie
briefings.tldr: Pete Hegseth joined Kentucky congressional candidate and retired Navy SEAL Ed Gallrein on the campaign trail, rallying voters to support a military-focused "America First" agenda while sharply criticizing incumbent Representative Thomas Massie as an obstructionist who fails to back Donald Trump.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Pete Hegseth joined Kentucky congressional candidate and retired Navy SEAL Ed Gallrein on the campaign trail, rallying voters to support a military-focused "America First" agenda while sharply criticizing incumbent Representative Thomas Massie as an obstructionist who fails to back Donald Trump.

---

## Ed Gallrein’s Transition from Combat to Congress
* **Extensive Military Career:** Ed Gallrein is a retired Navy SEAL with three decades of service, including leadership within the elite SEAL Team 6. 
    * He is one of the few SEALs to earn an Army Ranger qualification and the only Navy SEAL to earn the Army Combat Parachutist Badge.
    * His decorations include four Bronze Stars and two prestigious Presidential Unit Citations.
* **Deep Local Roots:** Gallrein is a fifth-generation Kentucky dairy farmer whose family has worked their land for over a century.
* **Motivation for Office:** Gallrein emphasized his desire to bring real-world leadership to Washington, expressing frustration with career politicians who make life-or-death decisions for troops without ever having served themselves.
    * **The "Secret Weapon":** Gallrein called regular American patriots the nation's true "secret weapon," far more powerful than elite military units or classified technology.

## Critique of Incumbent Representative Thomas Massie
* **Accusations of Obstructionism:** Speaker Pete Hegseth leveled strong criticism against incumbent Representative Thomas Massie, arguing that Massie’s constant opposition has crossed from principled conservatism into mere obstruction.
    * **The Trump Contrast:** Hegseth stated that Donald Trump does not need party members who constantly debate process or vote with Democrats during critical legislative moments; he needs loyal "reinforcements."
* **Grandstanding vs. Governing:** Hegseth contrasted Gallrein’s military record of action under pressure with Massie’s tenure, characterizing Massie’s career as "grandstanding" and "acting like being difficult is the same thing as being courageous."
* **Voting Record Discrepancies:** Ashley Hayek, President of America First Works, highlighted that some self-proclaimed "America First" politicians—alluding to Massie—voted against crucial legislation like the Working Family Tax Cuts, which funded southern border security and military modernization.

## Rebuilding Military Culture and Combat Readiness
* **Rejecting "Woke" Ideology:** Both Gallrein and Hegseth argued that under the Biden administration, the U.S. military shifted its focus away from warfighting and toward progressive social engineering.
    * **Specific Grievances:** They criticized the implementation of diversity quotas, pronoun mandates, gender identity policies, and climate change seminars within the armed forces.
* **Restoring the Warrior Ethos:** Gallrein and Hegseth emphasized that the sole mission of the military must be lethality, readiness, and winning the nation's wars.
    * They argued that restoring traditional, merit-based standards has already begun to turn around recent historic lows in military recruiting and retention.
* **Deterrence Through Strength:** Echoing the peace-through-strength philosophy of Ronald Reagan, Gallrein asserted that U.S. adversaries like China, Russia, and Iran are only deterred when they fear American military might.

## The Push for "America First" Unity in Washington
* **The Need for Congressional Backing:** Hegseth urged Kentucky voters to send "warriors" rather than "commentators" to Washington to support Donald Trump's policy agenda.
* **Defending the Border and Economy:** America First Works highlighted key policy priorities of their platform, including securing the southern U.S. border, eliminating taxes on tips, overtime, and Social Security, and driving national defense modernization.
* **Unified Front:** The rally speakers called on conservative voters to prioritize unity over internal party bickering to successfully combat radical left-wing policies.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "The military I first served in under President Reagan was built around one simple principle: Fight and win our nation's wars. That was mission first. Not politics, not ideology, not social experiments."  
> — **Ed Gallrein**

> "At some point, being against everything becomes an excuse for accomplishing nothing. At some point, constant obstruction is not leadership, it's just commentary."  
> — **Pete Hegseth**

> "We are telling young Americans once again that the military is not a social club, it is not a political activist organization, it is a warrior institution dedicated to defending the United States of America."  
> — **Ed Gallrein**

> "There's a massive, a massive difference between those who talk about leadership and people who actually lead. Trust me, we already have plenty of talkers in DC."  
> — **Pete Hegseth**

briefings.title: FULL SPEECH: JD Vance speaks at Kansas City manufacturing facility
briefings.tldr: JD Vance emphasizes a "workers-first" economic agenda focused on revitalizing American manufacturing, slashing government fraud, and prioritizing the safety and financial security of U.S. citizens over illegal immigrants.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
JD Vance emphasizes a "workers-first" economic agenda focused on revitalizing American manufacturing, slashing government fraud, and prioritizing the safety and financial security of U.S. citizens over illegal immigrants.

## Manufacturing and Economic Recovery
* **Commitment to American Workers:** Vance praises the employees at Milbank Manufacturing for their dedication during the pandemic, contrasting those who "sat at home on a laptop" with essential workers who continued to build the country’s infrastructure.
* **Investment in Domestic Production:** He argues that under the leadership of Donald Trump and Congressional Republicans, the U.S. has pivoted from "shedding jobs" to "creating jobs."
    * **Job Growth:** Claims the economy added 123,000 jobs last month and saw the largest growth in manufacturing employment since the first Trump term.
    * **Reshoring Industry:** Vows to end the era of shipping jobs to Mexico and China by making it "great to build in the United States once again."

## Legislative Contrast and Tax Policy
* **Working Families Tax Cuts:** Highlights legislation authored by Congressman Jason Smith aimed at putting more money in the pockets of Missourians.
    * **Partisan Divide:** Criticizes Congressional Democrats for largely voting against these tax cuts and $30 billion in funding intended to save rural healthcare clinics.
* **Critique of the Democratic Party:** Vance asserts that the modern Democratic Party has moved away from its "patriotic" roots, claiming leadership is more beholden to Nancy Pelosi and special interest groups than to working-class families.
* **Candidate Loyalty:** Warns voters that Democratic candidates may campaign as moderates but will ultimately "fall in line" with party leadership once in Washington.

## The Fraud Task Force and Public Accountability
* **Combating Systemic Fraud:** Vance discusses his role leading a fraud task force, describing the effort to root out corruption in Washington as "fishing in a barrel with a nuclear weapon."
* **Protecting Public Programs:** Emphasizes that fraud is not a victimless crime, as it steals from taxpayers and deprives intended beneficiaries of services.
    * **Specific Targets:** Highlights theft within the Medicaid and Medicare programs, as well as food stamp fraud.
    * **Recent Prosecution:** Mentions a recent case in the Western District of Missouri where a fraudster was sent to prison for identity theft and writing bad checks.
* **Ethical Mandate:** Asserts a simple principle: public officials who fail to fight fraud or individuals who steal from the American people belong in prison.

## Border Security and National Safety
* **National Priorities:** Recalls an incident from the State of the Union where he claims Democrats "sat on their hands" rather than cheering for a girl wounded by an illegal alien criminal or for the principle of a closed border.
* **Law Enforcement Support:** Advocates for empowering local police to combat violent crime.
    * **Personal Context:** Relates the need for safety to his upbringing in Middletown, Ohio, noting that while wealthy citizens can afford private security, working-class families rely on public safety to thrive.
* **Core Representation:** Argues that the fundamental difference between the parties is who they represent: Republicans for American citizens and Democrats for "illegal aliens and fraudsters."

> "We decided to put American businesses and most importantly American workers first for a change. We decided to fight for you instead of fight against you which is what way too many leaders have been doing." — JD Vance

> "If you are committing fraud against the American people, you ought to go to prison. If you are a public official and you're not fighting against fraud, you ought to have your money taken away." — JD Vance

> "I’m not asking you to vote for Republicans because we’re right about everything... I’m asking you to vote for Republicans because at least we know who we fight for. And we fight for you." — JD Vance

briefings.title: How Founders Can Build for Law Enforcement and First Responders | The a16z Show

people.name: Jeffrey Glover
people.role: Director, Arizona Department of Public Safety

briefings.tldr: Public safety is undergoing a paradigm shift toward a data-driven "ecosystem" where autonomous drones, AI-powered sensor networks, and officer wellness analytics are replacing traditional, reactive policing models to solve staffing shortages and improve de-escalation.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Public safety is undergoing a paradigm shift toward a data-driven "ecosystem" where autonomous drones, AI-powered sensor networks, and officer wellness analytics are replacing traditional, reactive policing models to solve staffing shortages and improve de-escalation.

## The Shift to Autonomous First Response
The integration of drones and sensors is transforming how departments handle high-risk situations by providing immediate, low-cost situational awareness.

*   **Drone-as-First-Responder (DFR):** Rahul Sidhu (Flock Safety) notes that drones act as flying robots capable of automating tasks like chasing Amber Alert vehicles or pursuing shooters detected by gunshot sensors. 
    *   **Sustainability:** Replacing traditional helicopters with drones is more cost-effective; maintaining 24/7 aerial coverage with helicopters is financially impossible for most departments.
*   **De-escalation via Intelligence:** David Ulevitch cites an example where a drone identified a "man with a shotgun" as actually being a "janitor with a broom," preventing a potentially violent police confrontation through superior situational awareness.
*   **Layered Sensor Networks:** Flock Safety utilizes a combination of license plate readers (LPR), gunshot detection, and drone dispatch to create a proactive safety net.

## AI and Officer Wellness
Colonel Jeffrey Glover (Arizona DPS) highlights a shift toward using technology to support the "human" element of policing, specifically focusing on mental health and performance optimization.

*   **Brain Scan Diagnostics:** Arizona DPS utilizes **Vytania (Heal the Heroes)** to conduct brain scans as "temperature checks" for officers to assess mental readiness.
*   **Body-Worn Camera Analytics:** The department uses **Truleo** to run analytics on body-cam footage.
    *   **Behavioral Scorecards:** The tech tracks how troopers interact with the public and vice versa.
    *   **Burnout Detection:** The system flags signs of officer burnout or high-stress levels, allowing supervisors to intervene before a crisis occurs.
*   **Structural Support:** Based on tech-driven burnout data, the department has instituted well-checks and sabbaticals at the 15-year and 25-year marks to maintain job satisfaction.

## Global Intelligence and Large-Scale Events
As global events increasingly have local repercussions, law enforcement is expanding its intelligence apparatus beyond local borders.

*   **Fusion Centers:** The **Arizona Counter Terrorism Information Center (ACTIC)** collaborates with other U.S. fusion centers to share unclassified data on global crime trends.
*   **International Partnerships:** Colonel Glover is building intelligence-sharing bridges with nations including Mexico (Sonora), the UAE, and Liberia to stay ahead of international criminal trends.
*   **Major Event Readiness:** Departments are currently utilizing the **TRX program** to prepare for high-security upcoming events like the FIFA World Cup and the Olympics.

## Advice for Public Safety Founders
Building for law enforcement requires a high degree of empathy and a willingness to navigate a culture that is famously resistant to change.

*   **The "Dual Hate" Paradox:** Rahul Sidhu notes that "Cops hate two things: for things to change and for things to stay the same." Founders must navigate this narrow path by building tools that feel "inevitable."
*   **Immersion is Mandatory:** To build effective tools, founders must conduct ride-alongs or serve as reserve officers. Understanding the "language" and the feeling of being on the beat is critical for product-market fit.
*   **The 10-Year Outlook:** Colonel Glover predicts that within a decade, the officer skill set will shift from physical tactics (e.g., "kicking in doors") to more nuanced, investigative work focused on AI-driven fraud and technical video analysis.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "There's two things cops hate: for things to change and for things to stay the same." — **Rahul Sidhu**, Co-founder of Flock Safety

It's going to be looking at the technical aspects of this video you just received and looking at AI and certain things that are going to come up from a fraud standpoint." — **Colonel Jeffrey Glover**, Director of Arizona Department of Public Safety

briefings.title: LIVE: Vice President JD Vance Delivers Remarks To Promote American Manufacturing In Kansas City, MO
briefings.tldr: Vice President JD Vance visited Milbank manufacturing in Kansas City to promote the administration’s "America First" economic agenda, highlighting a resurgence in domestic manufacturing and his ongoing leadership of a federal task force dedicated to rooting out government waste and fraud.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Vice President JD Vance visited Milbank manufacturing in Kansas City to promote the administration’s "America First" economic agenda, highlighting a resurgence in domestic manufacturing and his ongoing leadership of a federal task force dedicated to rooting out government waste and fraud.

## Economic Growth and Manufacturing Resurgence
* **Manufacturing Investment:** Vance highlighted that the administration’s policies have shifted the national narrative from shedding jobs to creating them, specifically noting significant growth in manufacturing employment over the last quarter.
* **Labor Statistics:** The Vice President cited a recent addition of 123,000 jobs nationally, which he attributed to deliberate decisions to prioritize American workers over global economic interests.
* **The "Milbank" Example:** Vance praised workers at the Milbank manufacturing facility for their essential labor during the COVID-19 pandemic, contrasting them with workers who remained at home on laptops.
* **Pro-Growth Policy:** The briefing emphasized that "putting American workers first" has led to a construction and manufacturing recovery that exceeded economists' expectations.

## Legislative and Tax Priorities
* **Working Families Tax Cut:** Vance touted legislation authored by Congressman Jason Smith, describing it as the largest tax cut for working-class Missourians in U.S. history.
* **Rural Healthcare:** The administration supports $30 billion in funding aimed at preventing the closure of rural healthcare clinics, a measure Vance claimed was largely opposed by congressional Democrats.
* **Missouri Leadership:** Vance acknowledged local Republican leaders in attendance, including Senators Eric Schmitt and Roger Marshall, Governor Mike Kehoe, and Congressmen Jason Smith and Mark Alford.
* **Redistricting:** Recognition was given to Governor Kehoe for his role in creating Missouri’s brand-new 5th Congressional District, where the event was held.

## The Federal Fraud Task Force
* **Mission Overview:** Vance detailed his role leading a task force focused on prosecuting waste, fraud, and abuse. He described finding fraud in Washington as "fishing in a barrel with a nuclear weapon."
* **Specific Targets:** 
    * **Program Integrity:** The task force is targeting theft from the Medicaid ($1.4 billion identified in one instance), Medicare, and food stamp programs.
    * **Accountability:** Vance noted a recent prosecution in the Western District of Missouri involving a fraudster from Detroit who was stealing check information and identities.
* **Philosophical Approach:** Vance argued that government generosity depends on the rule of law, stating that fraudsters "taking food from the mouths of poor children" must face prison time to preserve public trust.

## Partisan Critique and National Vision
* **State of the Union Reflection:** Vance criticized congressional Democrats for "sitting on their hands" during the State of the Union, specifically regarding border security and the recognition of a young victim of a crime committed by an undocumented immigrant.
* **National Identity:** He framed the administration's mission as a restoration of a government that serves its own citizens rather than "illegal alien criminals" or "left-wing NGOs."
* **Personal Narrative:** Drawing on his upbringing in Middletown, Ohio, and his "Mamaw" and "Papaw," Vance promised to view policy through the eyes of the working class, focusing on preventing jobs from being shipped to Mexico and China.

> "America isn't just some economic zone. America is a people, it's a nation... We’re restoring a government that serves its own people again." — **Vice President JD Vance**

> "If you're committing fraud against the American people, you ought to go to prison. If you are a public official and you're not fighting against fraud, you ought to have your money taken away." — **Vice President JD Vance**

> "We decided to put American businesses and, most importantly, American workers first for a change. We decided to fight for you instead of fight against you." — **Vice President JD Vance**

briefings.title: Nvidia’s CEO Says China Will Open Its Market to AI Chips From US
briefings.tldr: The AI industry is shifting from generative content to "Agentic AI"—digital workers capable of performing complex tasks on-premise.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The AI industry is shifting from generative content to "Agentic AI"—digital workers capable of performing complex tasks on-premise. This transition is driving massive enterprise demand for integrated "AI Factories" that currently exceeds global supply capacity.

## The Shift to Agentic AI and Enterprise Production
* **From Testing to Production:** Michael Dell noted that the market has moved beyond evaluation. Major enterprises like Eli Lilly and Samsung are now deploying AI in production environments using thousands of GPUs.
* **Defining Agentic AI:** Jensen Huang distinguished between early generative AI (which creates content) and "Agentic AI," which performs productive work. He views these agents as digital workers that reason, plan, and use tools.
* **On-Premise Necessity:** While early AI resided in the cloud, enterprise intelligence is moving "on-prem." 
    * **Data Security:** Companies want agents near their proprietary and secure data.
    * **Contextual Intelligence:** Intelligence must be produced at the point of action (e.g., in a factory, hospital, or car) to be effective.

## Reimagining Hardware: The "AI Factory"
* **The Concept of the "Harness":** Huang described a hardware/software "harness" that wraps around a Large Language Model (LLM) to turn a "brain" into an agent. 
    * This harness allows the model to access memory, networks, and local "scratchpad" memory to execute tasks.
* **CPU Importance:** Contrary to the focus on GPUs, Agentic AI requires significant CPU power. 
    * **Tool Usage:** While the GPU serves as the "brain," CPUs act as the harness that allows agents to interface with digital tools and management systems.
* **Integrated Solutions:** Dell is positioning itself as the primary channel for the "Dell AI Data Platform," integrating NVIDIA’s Grace Blackwell chips, NVLink networking, and NeMo Guardrails into a turnkey solution for enterprises.

## Supply Chain Constraints and Market Dynamics
* **Unprecedented Demand:** The supply chain is currently quadrupling capacity annually, yet demand continues to outstrip supply. Huang expects this build-out to last at least a decade.
* **Key Bottlenecks:** Primary constraints include advanced node semiconductors and high-bandwidth memory (HBM). 
* **Long-term Planning:** NVIDIA and Dell are coordinating with suppliers like Micron and SK Hynix on three-to-five-year roadmaps to ensure capacity for the transition from digital agents to physical AI (robotics).
* **Structural Change:** Both CEOs argue this is not a traditional "boom and bust" cyclical market but a fundamental structural shift in how the world consumes computing.

## Geopolitics: China and Taiwan
* **The China Market:** Huang expressed optimism that the Chinese market will eventually open further to US technology. 
    * **H200 Licensing:** NVIDIA’s H200 chips are licensed for sale in China, though the Chinese government is currently balancing local industry protection with the need for AI capacity.
* **Supply Resilience:** While Taiwan remains the "epicenter" of technology manufacturing, both companies are supporting "reindustrialization" in the United States.
    * **Diversity:** Efforts are underway to build more chip factories and packaging facilities in the US to create supply chain resilience.

## The Evolution of the PC: "Personal AI"
* **Beyond the Traditional PC:** The "Personal Computer" is evolving into "Personal AI." 
* **Local Context:** For individual productivity, AI must run locally on devices (like the Dell XPS) to access a user's specific context without needing to send all data to the cloud.
* **Productivity Gains:** Michael Dell noted that reimaging workflows with AI results in 10x to 100x improvements in speed, rather than incremental 10% gains.

## Notable Quotes

> "ChatGPT was fantastic, it launched generative AI... but doing work is really valuable. And now we're doing productive work incredibly well. That's why they're called agentic AI." — **Jensen Huang, CEO of NVIDIA**

> "When [companies] reimagine their workflows using this technology, they don't get 10 or 20 or 30 percent improvement, they get 10 times or 20 times or 100 times." — **Michael Dell, CEO of Dell Technologies**

> "We're going to have hundreds of millions of digital workers in the world. We're going to have billions of AI agents in the world and they're going to be working 24/7." — **Jensen Huang, CEO of NVIDIA**

> "Instead of personal computers, we're going to have personal AI... AI needs to be where the context is." — **Jensen Huang, CEO of NVIDIA**

briefings.title: The Inference Shift | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: The AI hardware market is shifting from a GPU-centric model focused on training to a heterogeneous landscape where "Agentic Inference"—autonomous tasks performed without human oversight—prioritizes massive memory capacity and low cost over raw processing speed.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The AI hardware market is shifting from a GPU-centric model focused on training to a heterogeneous landscape where "Agentic Inference"—autonomous tasks performed without human oversight—prioritizes massive memory capacity and low cost over raw processing speed.

## The State of AI Hardware: GPUs vs. Wafer-Scale
*   **The GPU Dominance:** Nvidia currently leads because GPUs excel at both training and inference by combining high compute power with High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) and sophisticated chip-to-chip networking.
    *   **Training Dynamics:** Training requires massive parallelization but is bottlenecked by serial steps where all GPUs must share results, making Nvidia’s networking a "moat."
    *   **The SpaceX/Anthropic Benchmark:** Anthropic’s deal to use SpaceX’s "Colossus 1" (220,000 Nvidia GPUs) illustrates how the same hardware is currently used interchangeably for both training and high-scale inference.
*   **Cerebras and the Speed Niche:** Cerebras’ WSE-3 chip bypasses traditional size limits by using an entire silicon wafer as a single chip, leading to extreme performance metrics.
    *   **Bandwidth Advantage:** The WSE-3 offers 21 petabytes per second of bandwidth—6,000 times that of an Nvidia H100.
    *   **The Trade-off:** While "blisteringly fast," Cerebras is limited by on-chip memory capacity (44GB SRAM). If a model or context (KV cache) exceeds this, the architecture becomes prohibitively expensive and inefficient.

## Defining the "Inference Shift"
*   **Answer Inference:** This is the current standard (e.g., ChatGPT, voice assistants). It is human-centric and highly sensitive to latency.
    *   **User Experience:** Speed is the primary variable. For "Answer Inference," chips like Cerebras or Groq are ideal because they minimize the time a human waits for a response.
*   **Agentic Inference:** This represents the next era, where AI agents (like Claude Code) perform complex, multi-step tasks autonomously.
    *   **Machine-to-Machine:** The true power of agents lies in work done without human involvement. If an agent runs a job overnight, the "tokens per second" speed is secondary to the agent's ability to complete the task.
    *   **Memory over Speed:** Agentic workloads require massive context, history, and state. This favors a "memory hierarchy" (DRAM, SSDs, databases) over pure compute speed.

## The Economic Unbundling of the GPU
*   **Stranded Resources:** Current GPU architectures often "strand" resources—wasting HBM during prefill or wasting compute during the serial decode process.
*   **The "Good Enough" Architecture:** Because agents are latency-tolerant, the market will likely shift toward cheaper, high-capacity memory and "good enough" compute.
    *   **Cost Efficiency:** Hyperscalers may favor simpler, non-GPU-bound systems for agentic workloads to reduce premiums paid for Nvidia’s high-speed networking and HBM.
    *   **Strategic Advantage for China:** China possesses the "good enough" components (older GPUs/CPUs and standard DRAM) required for agentic inference, potentially mitigating their lack of access to bleeding-edge nodes for training.

## Future Implications: Space and Moore's Law
*   **Space-Based Data Centers:** Slower, older nodes are actually better suited for space.
    *   **Reliability:** Physically larger transistors (older nodes) withstand radiation better.
    *   **Thermals:** Lower power consumption reduces the difficulty of dissipating heat in a vacuum.
*   **The End of Moore's Law Necessity:** While Nvidia’s Jensen Huang argues Moore's Law is dead to promote systems innovation, agentic inference suggests it might not matter at all. If the primary market for AI moves to autonomous agents, the industry can scale by adding more "good enough" compute rather than chasing marginal speed gains on the bleeding edge.

> "The true power of agents will not be that they do work for humans, but rather that they do work without human involvement at all." — **Ben Thompson**

> "Agentic inference will be the largest market by far, because that is the market that won't be limited by humans or time... the market size scales not with humans, but with compute." — **Ben Thompson**

> "Maybe the most profound implication of agents that act without humans in the loop... will be that Moore’s Law doesn't matter, and that the way we get more compute is by realizing that the compute we have is already good enough." — **Ben Thompson**

briefings.title: WATCH LIVE: Vance speaks at a manufacturing facility in Kansas City
briefings.tldr: Vice President JD Vance and Missouri Republican leaders gathered at Milbank Manufacturing to champion a "manufacturing-first" economic agenda, emphasizing the "Working Families Tax Cuts," aggressive anti-fraud initiatives, and a pivot away from global trade dependence toward domestic production.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Vice President JD Vance and Missouri Republican leaders gathered at Milbank Manufacturing to champion a "manufacturing-first" economic agenda, emphasizing the "Working Families Tax Cuts," aggressive anti-fraud initiatives, and a pivot away from global trade dependence toward domestic production.

## The Resurgence of American Manufacturing
*   **Milbank Manufacturing Case Study:** Speakers highlighted the 100-year-old family business as a symbol of American resilience for choosing to remain in the Midwest rather than offshoring to China.
*   **Economic Strategy:** The administration credited a "roaring" manufacturing comeback to bold tariffs, fair trade commitments, and the "Working Families Tax Cuts" that reward companies for building domestically.
*   **Kansas City’s Industrial Identity:** Congressman Mark Alford traced the city’s history from the 1821 fur trade and the first Ford Model T assembly plant to the current production of the Ford F-150 in Claycomo, arguing that a strong nation must "make things" to survive.
*   **National Independence:** Senator Eric Schmitt framed manufacturing as a "civilizational issue," arguing that dependency on foreign nations for steel, semiconductors, and pharmaceuticals compromises national security.

## Legislative and Tax Priorities
*   **Working Families Tax Cuts:** Congressman Jason Smith (Chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee) discussed authoring a "big beautiful bill" containing 103 tax provisions.
    *   **Target Demographics:** The bill specifically focuses on relief for overtime workers, tipped employees, and those on Social Security.
    *   **Development Process:** Smith noted that the legislation was drafted based on direct testimony from factory workers and small business owners in field hearings rather than Washington lobbyists.
*   **Trade Policy Reform:** The administration is targeting "non-tariff barriers" in the European Union. 
    *   **Market Disparities:** Smith highlighted that Honduras (10 million people) and Angola currently purchase more U.S. pork and chicken than the entire European Union due to restrictive EU trade policies.

## Anti-Fraud and Government Accountability
*   **Fraud Task Force:** Vice President JD Vance described his role leading a task force to root out waste, fraud, and abuse in government programs.
    *   **Scale of Corruption:** Vance characterized finding fraud in Washington as "fishing in a barrel with a nuclear weapon," citing a recent prosecution involving $1.4 billion stolen from Medicaid.
    *   **Specific Cases:** Mentioned a recent prosecution in the Western District of Missouri involving a Detroit-based fraudster and another case where a power of attorney stole $750,000 from a retired teacher.
*   **Accountability Measures:** The administration is pushing for prison sentences for those defrauding public programs like food stamps (SNAP) and Medicare, arguing that these crimes "steal food from the mouths of poor children."

## Public Safety and Border Security
*   **Border Enforcement:** Senator Schmitt and VP Vance asserted that the administration has secured the border, claiming illegal crossings have "collapsed" and that the government is prioritizing the deportation of illegal aliens over their "welcome."
*   **Law Enforcement Empowerment:** VP Vance attributed a historic drop in the murder rate—claiming it is at its lowest level in 127 years—to the administration’s focus on empowering local police and rejecting the "chaos" of the previous four years.
*   **Political Contrast:** Vance claimed a fundamental difference in priorities between parties, alleging that Congressional Democrats "relish fighting for illegal aliens" while Republicans prioritize the American citizenry.

## Notable Quotes
> "A nation cannot survive if it stops making things. For decades, too many leaders in this country treated American manufacturing like it was dispensable and disposable." — **Senator Eric Schmitt**

> "Fighting fraud in Washington, D.C., it's a little bit like fishing in a barrel with a nuclear weapon. It is the easiest thing to find." — **Vice President JD Vance**

> "We are turning the page to a new golden chapter of America... Let us all roll up our sleeves, fire up the machines, and build an America that every family can thrive [in]." — **Congressman Mark Alford**

> "I'm not asking you to vote for Republicans because we're right about everything... I'm asking you to vote for Republicans because at least we know who we fight for, and we fight for you." — **Vice President JD Vance**

briefings.title: Why Energy Stocks Are Down When They Should Be Up with Bob Brackett | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 60
briefings.tldr: The energy sector is currently defined by a "conundrum" where massive geopolitical supply shocks (specifically the Iranian threat to the Strait of Hormuz) haven’t translated into sustained stock rallies due to market belief in a quick resolution and a confusing forward curve.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The energy sector is currently defined by a "conundrum" where massive geopolitical supply shocks (specifically the Iranian threat to the Strait of Hormuz) haven’t translated into sustained stock rallies due to market belief in a quick resolution and a confusing forward curve. However, rising electricity demand for AI and data centers is creating a structural long-term growth story for natural gas and copper.

## The Oil Paradox and Geopolitical Risk
*   **The Strait of Hormuz "Black Swan":** Bob Brackett notes that Iran’s ability to block the Strait captures 20% of global oil flows and 20% of natural gas. This is a larger supply threat than the Russia-Ukraine war, yet oil prices remain below previous peaks due to "market hope" that the situation will be resolved quickly.
*   **The Inventory Drain:** Global inventories are being drained at a rate never seen before to compensate for supply shortfalls. This creates a "coiled spring" effect for prices as governments will eventually need to restock strategic reserves.
*   **The Forward Curve Confusion:** The market is currently in **Backwardation** (future prices are lower than spot prices). 
    *   Investors often mistakenly use the forward curve as a price predictor, leading them to fear negative earnings revisions and avoid stocks like ExxonMobil despite strong current cash flows.
*   **OPEC Instability:** The UAE's exit from the OPEC cartel stems from a desire to grow their prolific onshore resources, which was restricted by quotas. This signaling suggests a weakening of the cartel's long-term ability to control prices.

## Natural Gas: The AI and Electricity Growth Story
*   **Surging Electricity Demand:** After 15 years of flat demand, US electricity needs are growing at 3-4% annually, driven by AI data centers and robotics. 
    *   **Scale:** A single one-gigawatt data center requires as much energy as a city of one million people.
*   **The Bridge Fuel:** While nuclear is 24/7 "green," it has long lead times. Natural gas turbines are the only short-term solution to meet massive AI-driven power needs.
*   **Investment Picks:** Brackett favors "pure-play" dry gas producers over diversified majors for those looking to play the gas surge.
    *   **EQT (EQT) and Expand Energy (EXE):** These are the largest US gas producers and benefit most directly from rising Henry Hub prices.
*   **Negative Pricing in the Permian:** In West Texas, natural gas is currently a "waste product" with negative prices because oil drillers have no pipe capacity to move the associated gas, forcing them to pay others to take it away.

## Mining: Copper Scarcity vs. Lithium Disruption
*   **The Copper Tailwind:** Unlike oil (which benefited from fracking technology), there is no new technology to "frack" for copper. 
    *   **Freeport (FCX):** Identified as the "copper champion" due to its massive assets in Indonesia and the US.
    *   **Demand Drivers:** EVs and grid infrastructure are "copper-hungry." One EV contains as much copper as an entire house.
*   **Lithium’s Technological Shift:** Lithium is moving from traditional hard-rock mining to "oilfield brines."
    *   **The Arkansas/Appalachia Resource:** Companies like Exxon and Equinor are exploring extracting lithium from the salty water produced during oil and gas drilling. This "low-cost" chemical process could disrupt traditional lithium miners.

## Strategic Midstream and The "Toll-Booth" Model
*   **Cheniere Energy (LNG):** Described as a "refrigerator" model. They buy US gas, liquefy it, and sell it globally on 20-year "take-or-pay" contracts.
    *   **Safety:** It is a pass-through model that removes commodity price risk, acting as a "toll-booth" for global energy.
    *   **Valuation:** Currently trades at an 8% free cash flow yield, which Brackett views as undervalued compared to other S&P 500 midstream companies.
*   **The Majors (Exxon/Chevron):** These remain the "gold standard" for project management. Brackett notes their 3% dividends are "untouchable" and were maintained even when oil prices went negative during COVID, unlike European peers (Shell, BP) which cut distributions.

## Notable Quotes
> "When I tell you what I do [at a cocktail party] and you say, 'Let me refill my drink,' never to be seen again, then I know there’s an opportunity. When your ears perk up, that means we’re late cycle." — **Bob Brackett**

> "We've watched power demand in the US be flat for 15 years... suddenly, 3% growth on the electrical base is the equivalent of adding the electricity New York City consumes every year." — **Bob Brackett**

> "For those of you who are traders, this is where you want to dabble. For those who are growth stock investors, this is not where you want to be. These are trading vehicles, not long-term growth stocks." — **Steve Eisman**
